name: Teapot
baseMeaning: A teapot, the icon of tea ceremony and cozy comfort.
tldr: 🫖 means “I'm here for the tea”—watching the drama unfold from a safe distance, often with 👀.

contextMeanings.meaning: The sender wants the full story while keeping a safe distance from the drama.
contextMeanings.example: i'm just here for the tea 👀🫖

contextMeanings.meaning: The emoji comments on an overblown situation while implying that the sender is only observing it.
It can invite a playful retelling of relationship gossip without carrying a clearly romantic meaning.
contextMeanings.example: so what happened after you saw her message? 👀🫖

contextMeanings.meaning: In a literal plan, 🫖 can mean the sender is hosting a tea gathering rather than discussing office gossip.
contextMeanings.example: i'm bringing the teapot for our 3pm 🫖

platformNotes.note: In a private conversation, 🫖 often follows a screenshot or retelling of gossip. The 👀🫖 pairing makes the sender sound like an interested spectator rather than someone directly involved.
In comments beneath a dramatic post, 🫖 can show that the writer wants the story behind what is happening. It reads more like “I'm following this closely” than a literal reference to tea.
A TikTok reply to a video with unfolding conflict can use 🫖 to mark the commenter's place on the sidelines. Adding 👀 strengthens the sense that they are watching the mess develop.
In a group chat, 🫖 can turn a friend's dramatic recap into a request for the remaining details. It works especially well after several people already know the setup.

generationalNotes.note: Many younger users treat 🫖 as shorthand for “I'm here for the tea,” especially when it follows 👀 or an invitation to share gossip.
Some Gen X users read 🫖 as a humorous spectator reaction, though they may also recognize its more literal connection to hosting tea.
A boomer recipient may take 🫖 more literally because of its traditional tea association. The surrounding message matters when telling apart an actual invitation from gossip commentary.

warnings.title: Mistaken for a tea invitation
warnings.description: A sender using 🫖 to watch drama may be taken literally, especially in a family or work conversation. Say “I'm here for the story” when the gossip meaning is important.

seoDescription: What does 🫖 mean? It usually means “I'm here for the tea”—watching a messy situation unfold from a safe distance rather than literally offering tea.

longForm.overview:
🫖 can look like a polite invitation to make tea, but in a chat it often means “I'm here for the tea”: I am watching the drama, and I want the story without getting dragged into it. The 👀🫖 combination makes that intention especially clear. The sender is perched at a safe distance, following events unfold.

The glyph itself is a teapot, so its literal associations are tea, ritual, and comfort. Unlike 🍵, which is the drink itself, 🫖 is the vessel and the gathering around it. That is why 🫖 beside a plan to host someone, share a quiet moment, or celebrate a cozy occasion can still work. But once someone starts recounting scandal, conflict, or an absurd group-chat development, the emoji shifts from the object being discussed to the sender's role as an interested spectator. It is less “have some tea” than “tell me everything.”
longForm.howPeopleUseIt:
It appears when a friend forwards a screenshot of an awkward reveal, posts “you won't believe what happened,” or drops a dramatic group-chat update. Pairing it with 👀 makes the sender's position clear: they are watching from the edge and waiting for the rest of the story. A standalone 🫖 after the story says “I'm invested.”

It can also open a gossip exchange, especially when several people already know the setup. “Spill the tea” and “👀🫖” ask for details; a follow-up 🫖 after the explanation signals that the story landed. The joke is wanting the mess without joining the argument.
longForm.whenNotToUse: 🫖 can misfire when the conversation is genuinely about hosting tea. If you write “I'm bringing 🫖 for Saturday afternoon” and the other person has invited guests, the emoji may sound like an odd substitute for a cup or a plan to meet. Spell out “I'll bring the teapot and cups” instead. It can also feel too detached when someone is asking for direct emotional support; watching the drama from a safe distance is not the same as comforting the person involved. Use plain words when the person needs a response: “I'm here for you” or “tell me what you need.”
longForm.howToReply:
To match the tone, send 👀🫖, ask “what did I miss?”, or request the full story with “spill the tea.” A second 🫖 after the explanation says the drama was worth the update. If the sender is teasing you, keep the exchange light and ask for the part they left out.

If 🫖 appears on your own post, treat it as a sign that somebody wants to watch what happens next. Ask whether they want the inside story, or let their “I'm here for the tea” stand. If you actually meant a literal tea invitation, clarify that immediately so nobody mistakes your plan for gossip commentary.

faqs.question: What does 🫖 mean from a guy
faqs.answer: It does not prove romantic interest by itself. A guy sending 🫖 may be asking for gossip, watching drama, or teasing you with “spill the tea”; the surrounding message matters more than the emoji alone.

faqs.question: Is 🫖 flirty
faqs.answer: It can be playful in a dating chat, but it is not inherently flirty. The emoji usually asks for the story, so romantic intent has to come from the words around it.

faqs.question: What does 🫖 mean on TikTok
faqs.answer: On TikTok, 🫖 often means “I'm here for the tea,” especially beside 👀. It marks the commenter as someone watching the drama from a safe distance rather than taking a direct role in it.

faqs.question: Is 🫖 just about tea
faqs.answer: Not always. It can refer literally to a teapot or tea gathering, but in conversation it commonly means that someone wants the gossip behind an event.

conversationExamples.message: wait i need the whole story 👀🫖
conversationExamples.interpretation: The friend wants the details of a dramatic development without participating in it. Reply with the missing context or ask what happened next.

conversationExamples.message: so what happened after you saw her message 👀🫖
conversationExamples.interpretation: This is a playful request for a relationship update, not automatically a romantic signal. Match the teasing by asking for the version they have not told you yet.

conversationExamples.message: are we still on for the 3pm or should i bring the teapot 🫖
conversationExamples.interpretation: Here 🫖 is being used literally as part of a meeting or hosting plan. Confirm the time and say whether the teapot is a joke so nobody misreads the logistics.

conversationExamples.message: uncle james just announced he's selling the farm 👀🫖
conversationExamples.interpretation: The family-group message treats the announcement as drama worth watching from a distance. Respond with surprise or ask which relative heard it first.

conversationExamples.message: the comments on this post are a disaster 👀🫖
conversationExamples.interpretation: The sender is following the controversy unfolding in the comments. You can ask what they think is the wildest part or share the comment that started it.
